summary.intent: Triage and resolve CodeRabbit CLI review findings on a committed CipherBox FUSE phase, fixing valid issues and dismissing false positives.
summary.outcome: Removed one dead unreachable guard in content_ops.rs, corrected file-count arithmetic and post-revert accuracy in 4 planning docs, and confirmed the MAJOR inode.rs finding was a false positive. All 95 FUSE unit tests passed; changes committed.

repo: Phase 59 planning docs (SUMMARY, VALIDATION, PATTERNS, PLAN) still described the pre-revert strict-equality endpoint after a post-revert amendment was recorded only in VERIFICATION.md and UAT.md — doc accuracy drifts when amendments are added to some files but not others.

PATTERNS.md header said '8 modified Rust files' but footer said '9 source files'; the discrepancy was because the vector test lives under tests/ not crates/fuse/src/, so the scan-scope count was wrong.

Raw IPNS private keys are never carried in folder-metadata FilePointers — they are unwrapped from encrypted hex on re-resolution, so None for file_ipns_private_key in the pointer-change path is correct behavior, not a bug.

code.finding: current_seq.is_none() guard was unreachable in the else branch because current_seq was always Some(...) when is_first_publish == false; dead guard removed as part of D.3 cleanup.

CodeRabbit flagged the same_pointer==false path as failing to initialize key material, but lines 659 and 666 correctly set file_meta_ipns_name and file_ipns_key_encrypted_hex from the new pointer — false positive.

workflow: CodeRabbit MAJOR severity ratings can be false positives on crypto/key-management code where the reviewer misreads ownership vs. initialization semantics — always read the surrounding context before acting.
Splitting the code fix commit from planning-doc reconciliation commits produces a cleaner changelog when the changes are logically independent.
Generated FFI bindings (fuse_abi.rs) and test mocks produce pre-existing compiler warnings unrelated to edits — verify warning source before treating as regression.

friction: CodeRabbit's MAJOR finding required manual code reading to confirm as false positive — no way to dismiss it in the tool without investigation.
Post-revert amendments were recorded in VERIFICATION.md/UAT.md but not propagated to SUMMARY/VALIDATION/PATTERNS/PLAN, creating inconsistent doc state that CodeRabbit surfaced as review findings.
open_items: The 4 planning docs were corrected with amendment notes rather than full rewrites — they still describe the pre-revert strict-equality endpoint as the original design intent, which may confuse future readers.
phase uat-passed CLI handler remains unimplemented (pre-existing); workaround of editing VERIFICATION.md + phase complete is still in use.
